elevated-helideck-vertical-takeoff/intro.text: Two elevated-helideck profiles exist: Limited Exposure (performance permits continued OEI flight except for an engine failure very early in the takeoff, which may require a forced landing) and No Exposure (continued OEI flight or landing is available at all times when operating at the Figure 3-28 WAT conditions, which eliminates the risk of a forced landing). This page covers the Limited Exposure profile (Figure 3-22 WAT).
elevated-helideck-vertical-takeoff/intro.note: p.III-1-50 (DOC 633) ELEVATED HELIDECK TAKEOFF AND LANDING: Limited Exposure (continued OEI flight except early engine failure, forced landing might be required; Figure 3-22 WAT) and No Exposure (continued OEI flight or landing at all times; Figure 3-28 WAT eliminates the risk of a forced landing). FIXED 2026-09-26: said No Exposure was 'at a more restrictive weight', which the RFM does not say. Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-26.

elevated-helideck-vertical-takeoff/cauti.text: The nose wheel will not self-center after liftoff if it has swiveled about 180° just before liftoff. If retracted in this position, the nose wheel will jam in the up position and normal extension will not be possible. If swiveled more than 90°, taxi forward slightly to align it with the fuselage.
elevated-helideck-vertical-takeoff/cauti.note: p.III-1-50 (DOC 633) CAUTION: nose wheel will not self-center after lift-off if swiveled about 180°; jams up and normal extension will not be possible; more than 90° taxi forward slightly. Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-26.
